official.deadline_note: No central deadline is published. Each fellowship is announced as its own call for expressions of interest with its own closing date on WIPO's Taleo career site and on WIPO's LinkedIn or other social media channels. When the Taleo fellowship job list was checked on 10 October 2026 it displayed no currently advertised vacancy, so timing depends entirely on when a call opens.
official.application_cycle: Rolling, per vacancy: positions are advertised individually as calls for expressions of interest on WIPO's career website, LinkedIn and other social media channels, so there is no single annual application window.
official.status_note: The programme page is live and describes the fellowship as ongoing, but openings exist only as separate calls for expressions of interest, so availability depends on the current call rather than on a programme-wide round.
official.tuition_coverage_note: No tuition is covered: fellows work under a fellowship contract rather than studying, and the page publishes no tuition benefit.
benefits: Monthly stipend ranging from 3,000 to 8,000 CHF per month depending on your academic background and experience that may be relevant to the nature of the fellowship
Contract duration up to 12 months, with the possibility of renewal for a total of up to three years

Comprehensive medical and professional accident insurance coverage; WIPO pays 100% of the medical insurance premium for contracts of less than 12 months, 75% for contracts of 12 months or more, and 100% of the professional accident insurance premium
Relocation assistance: WIPO covers travel expenses at the start and end of the fellowship and, if necessary, assists in facilitating the visa formalities to Switzerland
10 days of official holidays per year plus 2.5 days of annual leave for each full month of the fellowship
Access to internal training programmes offered by the WIPO Academy, up to six study leave days per year, and WIPO bearing the cost of UN Official languages training where required by job duties
eligibility: At least a first-level university degree (e.g., a bachelor's degree)
Depending on the fellowship category, additional requirements such as a minimum level of professional experience, advanced degrees (Master or PhD) or specific competencies
No specific age limit for the fellowships
No limit on time since graduation: the fellowships are envisaged for young professionals and there is no specific period after graduation to apply
Former interns are welcome to apply provided they meet the eligibility criteria

Young Experts Program participants are not allowed to apply for any position at WIPO during a waiting period after finishing the programme - the programme page states one year and the FAQ states two years
requirements: At least a first-level university degree, for example a bachelor's degree
Any category-specific requirements stated in the individual call for expressions of interest, such as professional experience, an advanced degree or specific competencies
Excellent knowledge of written and spoken English, since exchanges at WIPO are primarily in English
Availability to work on-site in Geneva, Switzerland: WIPO does not offer remote fellowship opportunities
selection_criteria: Each call for expressions of interest is assessed against that category's own requirements, which may include a minimum level of professional experience, an advanced degree or specific competencies
Successful candidates need to demonstrate an excellent knowledge of written and spoken English
The programme page publishes no selection weighting between criteria
coverage: Monthly stipend of CHF 3,000 to CHF 8,000 depending on academic background and experience relevant to the nature of the fellowship
Travel expenses at the start and at the end of the fellowship
Medical insurance premium (100% for contracts under 12 months, 75% for contracts of 12 months or more) and 100% of the professional accident insurance premium
Visa facilitation to Switzerland for the selected fellow; no relocation allowance and no accommodation are provided
application_method: Monitor WIPO's career website, LinkedIn and other social media channels for calls for expressions of interest
Open the relevant call and submit an expression of interest through WIPO's Taleo career site
Meet the category-specific requirements set out in that individual call
official.application_route: Apply online through WIPO's Taleo career portal to an individual published call for expressions of interest; there is no year-round open application.
official.study_mode: Full-time, on-site in Geneva, Switzerland; remote fellowships are not offered
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality or residency restriction is published on the programme page; WIPO assists the selected fellow with visa formalities to Switzerland, and fellows remain responsible for local taxation and social security obligations arising from their contract.
official.international_eligibility: No nationality limit is published; fellows come from many countries and WIPO facilitates the fellow's own visa, but visa assistance is not extended to family members, who also receive no Swiss legitimation card.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Four categories: translation fellows (PCT Translation and Terminology Fellowship Program, for assistant terminologists, translators, post-editors, translation technologists and technical specialists), legal case manager fellows (WIPO Domain Name Fellowship Program, for young law graduates), visiting and research fellows (Research and Visiting Fellowship Program, for backgrounds in economics or statistics) and other specialized fellows.
official.duration: 12 to 36 months in total; contracts run up to 12 months with one or more extensions, provided the maximum cumulative length does not exceed three years
official.description: WIPO's Fellowship Program offers professionals the opportunity to gain hands-on experience, expand knowledge, build networks and contribute to global innovation and creativity in intellectual property and international cooperation at the Organization's Geneva headquarters. Fellows are classified into four categories based on the functions performed and WIPO's business needs, and are placed for 12 to 36 months.
official.program_type: Professional fellowship programme of an international organization, with four fellow categories
official.english_requirement: Excellent knowledge of written and spoken English; no IELTS or TOEFL score is published

not_confirmed: funding_amount as a single figure - the page publishes only the range CHF 3,000-8,000 per month, so no single value can be quoted without misstating it
documents required - each individual call publishes its own document list
central deadline - none published; timing is per call
English test score - the requirement is stated qualitatively with no IELTS/TOEFL threshold published
verification.notes: Stipend wording, insurance percentages, relocation assistance, leave, training, duration, eligibility and the four fellow categories were taken from the official WIPO fellowship programme page; English, tax, stipend-freeze, extension, housing, family and outside-funding rules from the official programme FAQ page. The Taleo fellowship job list was checked and showed no advertised vacancy at verification time. Note the discrepancy on the Young Experts Program waiting period: the programme page says one year, the FAQ says two years.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a paid, Geneva-based work fellowship rather than a study grant: you apply to individual calls for expressions of interest on WIPO's Taleo portal whenever one opens, and your stipend level is fixed before you start and is maintained for the whole fellowship. Budget for Geneva yourself - WIPO pays only the start and end travel, contributes 75-100% of the medical premium, and offers no housing, no relocation allowance and no visa support for family members. Any outside stipend, grant, bursary or scholarship you hold must be declared and may be deducted from the WIPO stipend, and you remain liable for local taxes and social security.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Young professionals with at least a first university degree who want hands-on IP exposure in Geneva - translators and terminologists, law graduates for domain-name disputes, or economics and statistics graduates for research work.
application_readiness_checklist: Create and keep current a candidate profile on WIPO's Taleo fellowship portal so a call can be applied to within its short window
Prepare a reusable English CV, cover letter and certified degree records, since each call publishes its own document list
Read the category description in every call before applying; the four tracks screen on very different competencies
Build a Geneva budget showing how a stipend between CHF 3,000 and CHF 8,000 covers rent, insurance and taxes
Document any external funding you receive so you can declare it immediately, as it can be deducted from the stipend
Confirm your Young Experts Program cooling-off period with WIPO HR if you are a former YEP, since the two official pages state different lengths
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a category that does not match your profile: each of the four tracks screens on different degrees, experience and competencies
Missing a call because openings are announced ad hoc on the career site and LinkedIn rather than in a fixed window
Weak written or spoken English despite strong academic records - the FAQ makes excellent English a hard requirement
Applying while still inside the Young Experts Program waiting period, which blocks any WIPO position
Expecting the fellowship to convert into a WIPO staff job - it does not guarantee future employment
Assuming the full CHF 8,000 rate: the stipend is set individually before the start and stays flat, with no increase on extension
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Geneva rent and daily living costs, local taxes and social security, health insurance for children (not covered), family visas, and any travel beyond the start and end relocation trips.
document_audit: Each call publishes its own required documents - do not reuse the same attachment set blindly for every vacancy
Your degree level must match the category: some tracks ask for professional experience, a Master's or PhD, or specific competencies
Former interns may apply freely, but former YEP participants must serve the full waiting period first
alerts: There is no central deadline: a call can open and close at any time, so the Taleo portal must be monitored directly
The stipend is frozen for the duration of the fellowship, including after any extension
Remuneration, grants, bursaries or scholarships from any other source must be declared and may reduce the WIPO stipend
Remote work is not an option - most positions are at the Geneva headquarters
The programme page and the FAQ disagree on the YEP waiting period (one year versus two years), so verify before relying on either
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online through the WIPO Taleo career portal against a specific published call; WIPO screens candidates against that call's requirements and warns that replies to unsuccessful applicants can take longer because of the programme's pace.

official.deadline_note: The fellowship deadline is the EPFL Bachelor admission deadline: the corresponding box must be ticked on the Bachelor's application form before April 30th, and the registration form must be validated and paid by April 30 at the latest. The official pages state 'April 30th' without a year; 30 April 2027 is the next occurrence for the intake starting September 2027.
official.application_cycle: Annual, tied to EPFL Bachelor admission: applications can be submitted from mid-November to April 30 to start studies at EPFL the following September; results are communicated at the end of June.
official.status_note: The programme page is live for the current admission round: applications for the next intake open in mid-November and close on April 30, after which sections pre-select candidates for jury presentations and the central commission decides by the end of June.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The fellowship is published as a financial fellowship of CHF 10,000 spread over three years; the official pages do not describe it as covering tuition.
official.funding_period: total over 3 years, in 6 semester instalments
benefits: Financial support of CHF 10,000.-, divided into six instalments paid at the beginning of each semester to a Swiss bank or postal account
Payment schedule: CHF 2,000.- per semester in the first year and CHF 1,500.- per semester in the second and third years
Reservation of a room in an EPFL partner student residence (on request and at your own expense); the housing request is filled in the registration form
Certificate of excellence, delivered at the end of the curriculum
Cumulative with all other financial resources such as study grants or employment, with no effect on the payments or the amount
Access to the McCall MacBain Leadership Development Program, a three-year transversal-skills training pathway run in partnership with the McCall MacBain Foundation
eligibility: Anyone who has applied for admission to the EPFL Bachelor programme and meets one of the following: Swiss nationality or holder of a C permit; refugee or stateless status in Switzerland; holder of a certificate within the meaning of art. 1 of the ordinance concerning admission to EPFL; or a secondary II diploma obtained in Switzerland while domiciled in Switzerland
General average of the gymnasial maturity and the preceding year: minimum 5.3/6
Specific average of the scientific subjects and the maturity project: minimum 5/6
All specific options (OS) taken, with the reinforced mathematics level where applicable
For students who followed the CMS preparatory year: average of at least 5.00 at the end of the CMS
Eloquence, synthesis, engagement and the ability to put thoughts into perspective are also evaluated
requirements: Tick the corresponding box on the Bachelor's application form before April 30th and provide the requested application file
If eligible, return the ad hoc form sent by EPFL with the requested fellowship documents
Keep the semester registration confirmed and the semester invoice paid, as payments are conditional on both
Level B2 in French (C1 highly recommended) is required to follow EPFL Bachelor programmes; applicants who have not studied French must attest their level upon application
Pay the application fee: CHF 50.- for holders of a Swiss certificate or diploma, CHF 150.- for holders of a foreign certificate or diploma, by credit card, PayPal or Twint
documents: Secondary II transcripts covering the entire gymnasial curriculum
Summary of the maturity project ('travail de maturité') or an equivalent project, one page A4 maximum, in French or English
Motivation letter in French, English, German or Italian
Curriculum vitae including extracurricular activities, in French, English, German or Italian
Contact details of two referees: one science teacher and one person linked to an extracurricular activity or engagement, in French, English or German
selection_criteria: After Bachelor registrations close (April 30), each section pre-selects the best applications for a presentation of the maturity project, or another subject if not applicable, before a jury that includes members of EPFL's academic body
Eloquence, capacity for synthesis, engagement and the ability to put thoughts into perspective are evaluated during five-minute presentations followed by question and answer sessions
Selected applications are then examined by the Central Commission for Bachelor Excellence Fellowships, which awards the fellowships

Positive decisions are transmitted at the end of June subject to a final average matching the criteria; negative replies are communicated by the end of June at the latest and decisions are not subject to appeal
coverage: CHF 10,000 financial support paid in six semester instalments on a Swiss bank or postal account
CHF 2,000.- per semester in the first year, then CHF 1,500.- per semester in the second and third years
Reservation of a room in an EPFL partner student residence, at the student's own expense
Excellence certificate delivered at the end of the studies
No tuition coverage, travel support or living-cost guarantee is published
application_method: Complete, validate and pay the online Bachelor admission registration form
Tick the excellence fellowship box on that form before April 30 and fill in the housing request
If eligible, return the ad hoc form with transcripts, maturity project summary, motivation letter, CV and referee contacts
If pre-selected, present the maturity project before the section jury and await the central commission's decision at the end of June
official.application_route: Tick the excellence fellowship box on EPFL's online Bachelor admission form before April 30; shortlisted applicants then submit the fellowship dossier and present their maturity project before a jury.
official.citizenship_residency: Swiss nationality or C permit; refugee or stateless status in Switzerland; holder of a certificate within the meaning of art. 1 of the ordinance concerning admission to EPFL; or a secondary II diploma obtained in Switzerland while domiciled in Switzerland.
official.international_eligibility: Effectively limited to Switzerland-connected applicants: Swiss citizens or C permit holders, recognised refugees or stateless persons in Switzerland, holders of a certificate under art. 1 of the EPFL admission ordinance, or people who obtained their secondary II diploma in Switzerland while domiciled there. Holders of purely foreign school-leaving certificates do not qualify, even when they are admissible to EPFL.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: None: the fellowships are offered to students starting their Bachelor's degree regardless of the field of studies they choose.
official.research_requirement: A one-page A4 summary of the maturity project ('travail de maturité') or an equivalent project, in French or English, followed by an oral presentation before the jury for shortlisted candidates.
official.duration: Three years (Bachelor programme duration), with payments for a maximum of six semesters
official.description: In order to encourage holders of a Swiss high-school maturity diploma and holders of a Swiss vocational maturity diploma undertaking the CMS in their scientific ambitions, EPFL offers excellence fellowships to talented students starting their Bachelor's degree, regardless of the field of studies they choose. The fellowships reward candidates whose results and engagement stood out throughout their pre-university curriculum, in both school and extracurricular activities.
official.program_type: Merit-based excellence fellowship for students starting a first EPFL Bachelor, part of the 'Attract Talent' pillar of the EPFL Student Support Program

not_confirmed: english_requirement - no English test is published for the fellowship; the documents may be submitted in French, English, German or Italian, while the Bachelor programme itself requires French B2
number of fellowships awarded per year - not published
selection weighting between grade thresholds and the jury presentation - not published
verification.notes: Amount, instalment schedule, interruption rules, eligibility conditions, grade thresholds, required documents, jury process and decision timing were taken from the official EPFL 'Conditions d'admission & candidature' page; the CHF 10,000 over three years, guaranteed housing request and McCall MacBain complement from the English fellowship page; the April 30 application deadline, fee and French level requirement from the official Bachelor admission 'How to apply?' page. No aggregator or third-party source was used.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a CHF 10,000 merit fellowship for your first EPFL Bachelor, and it is effectively reserved for Switzerland-connected applicants: Swiss citizens or C-permit holders, recognised refugees or stateless persons in Switzerland, or people who took their secondary-II diploma in Switzerland. The money arrives in six semester instalments - CHF 2,000 per semester in year one, then CHF 1,500 in years two and three - and only while your semester registration is confirmed and its invoice paid. Read the 'guaranteed housing' as a reserved room you still pay for yourself, and note that payments stop if you are routed into the Mise a niveau course or fail the propaedeutic year.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Swiss or Swiss-domiciled final-year students with averages at or above 5.3/6 overall and 5/6 in science plus maturity work, strong extracurricular engagement, and the confidence to present their maturity project to a jury in French.
application_readiness_checklist: Compute both thresholds from your transcripts before applying: overall maturity average at least 5.3/6 and science-plus-maturity average at least 5/6
Diarise April 30: the fellowship box, the validated form and the payment all have to be done by that date
Write the one-page A4 maturity project summary in French or English and have it proofread to fit the page limit
Ask a science teacher and an extracurricular contact well in advance to act as referees
Rehearse a five-minute spoken presentation of your maturity project with follow-up questions, since eloquence and synthesis are scored
Fill in the student residence request in the registration form and budget the room rent separately from the CHF 10,000
common_rejection_risks: Forgetting to tick the fellowship box on the admission form - there is no separate fellowship application
Falling below either average threshold (5.3/6 overall or 5/6 for science and the maturity project)
A weak jury presentation: eloquence, synthesis and the ability to put thoughts into perspective are explicitly evaluated
Being oriented into the Mise a niveau course at the end of BA1 or failing the propaedeutic year at the end of BA2, which interrupts payments
Missing a semester registration confirmation or semester invoice payment, which suspends disbursement
Assuming foreign applicants qualify: only Swiss-connected candidates are eligible, and commission decisions cannot be appealed
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The reserved student-residence room rent (paid by the student), Lausanne living costs, semester fees and application fee, and everything beyond the CHF 10,000 over three years; this is a partial support, not a full ride.
document_audit: Transcripts must document the whole gymnasial curriculum, not just the final year
The maturity project summary is capped at one A4 page and accepted only in French or English
The motivation letter and CV may be in French, English, German or Italian, but referee contacts are requested in French, English or German
One of the two referees must be a science teacher; an extracurricular contact alone does not satisfy the requirement
The housing request belongs in the registration form, not in the later fellowship dossier
alerts: The deadline is the Bachelor admission deadline (April 30) for the following September intake - there is no separate fellowship round
Payments stop if you switch to the Mise a niveau track after BA1 or fail the propaedeutic year at the end of BA2; instalments already received are kept but the rest are lost
Decisions arrive at the end of June and the commission's decisions are not subject to appeal
The fellowship cannot be deferred or reported to a later year
French level B2 (C1 recommended) is a Bachelor admission requirement, so francophone applicants hold a practical advantage even though the fellowship itself sets no language test
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through EPFL's online Bachelor admission form with the fellowship box ticked and the fee paid by April 30; eligible candidates receive an ad hoc form for their dossier, sections pre-select for jury presentations, and the central commission communicates its decision at the end of June.
